messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: kv-cache-eviction-high on kv-cache-prod (shard-3, shard-8) fired at 2026-02-27T14:00:01Z  severity: page  runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/cache-hotkeys
Jamie: got page for evictions spike, paging rotation: I'm oncall until 14:15 UTC
Priya: looking at dashboards, global hit rate dip started ~13:58 UTC; shard-3 down to 9% hit, shard-8 to 22%.
Lina: any recent model or runtime pushes? deploy-bot shows no runtime deploys in last 24h, but a config change to kv-timeout went out yesterday.
Alex: can you pull top evicted keys per shard? also check write rate to KV and client IP distribution.
Priya: running quick query:
```
SELECT key_prefix, SUM(evictions) as evictions FROM cache_evictions WHERE shard IN ('shard-3','shard-8') GROUP BY key_prefix ORDER BY evictions DESC LIMIT 5;
-- results: user:session:abcdef ~3.2M, model:state:xyz ~800k, user:session:12345 ~400k
```
Priya: looks like a 'user:session:abcdef' prefix dominates shard-3.
Maya: support picked up several tickets reporting slow responses for generation endpoints. Ticket refs: #8593, #8594. I'm triaging.
Jamie: immediate mitigation: add temporary ingress rate-limit rule for that client prefix and create a temporary denylist in kv layer for that key to avoid thrashing.
Alex: agree. Do a conservative limit so we don't create 503s for other users. Add a circuit-breaker that returns a 429 for excessive prefix ops.
Priya: adding an alert tweak: current evictions alert is too chatty. I'm introducing a derivative-based rule and a precision filter for hot-key mutes. PromQL diff:
```
# old
sum(rate(cache_evictions_total[1m])) by (shard) > 5000
# new
increase(cache_evictions_total{shard=~"shard-.*"}[30s]) > 15000
OR
(clamp_max(cache_evictions_total, 1) / sum(cache_requests_total) by (shard)) > 0.25
```
Priya: also pushed a regex-based mute for key prefix 'user:session:abcdef' for 90m via PagerDuty API (mute id pd-mute-5543).
Lina: can we create a dashboard panel for 'hot-key ratio' and 'eviction-velocity' per-shard? I'll add small 1x2 panel and save snapshot.
Priya: done. Snapshot: https://grafana.redwood/internal/snapshot/hotkeys-20260227abcd
Alex: good. Also instrument a synthetic cache read for a small canary key every 15s and alert if >2 consecutive failures.
Maya: I notified the customer that we observed a heavy retry flow and asked them to pause for 30m while we stabilize. They acknowledged.
incident-bot: HANDOFF reminder: Jamie -> Alex at 14:15 UTC
Jamie: mitigation applied at ~14:05 UTC (ingress throttle + kv denylist). Evictions dropped from peak ~12k/s to ~400/s on shard-3.
Priya: metrics now: shard-3 hit rate up to 78%, shard-8 91%. Eviction velocity normalized. Created RFC ticket RFC-993: ingress-hotkey-isolation.
Alex: follow-ups: implement automated hot-key isolation that can detect a top-k storm and spin up per-prefix throttles at edge; also explore bloom-filter based admission to reduce churn.
Lina: I'll add runbook steps for "hot-key storm" including commands to mute by prefix, create PagerDuty mute, and add Grafana snapshot instructions.
Maya: support confirmations: affected customers updated, no SLA breach so far. I'll tag tickets and add customer-impact note in #customer-impact.
Priya: permanent alert changes applied, and added a 'noise-suppression' label to alerts to avoid duplicates. Also added a playbook link to the alert details.
Jamie: handing off to @Alex. Summary: hot-key client caused KV thrash across shard-3/8; applied ingress throttle + kv-level denylist; alerts retooled to look for velocity & hit-rate ratios; dashboards updated; follow-ups assigned.
Alex: taking over. Will run a short blameless postmortem if this repeats. tagging @oncall-rotation and @sre
incident-bot: Incident severity downgraded to 'investigating' and page cleared at 14:22 UTC. Timeline: page 14:00, throttle applied 14:05, mute 14:08, metrics stable 14:20.
Maya: logging action items: support follow-up (owner Maya), RFC-993 owner Alex (due next Tue), runbook update owner Lina (due EOD today), alert tuning owner Priya (DONE: committed rule changes).
Jamie: thanks everyone. I'll draft the short incident summary and attach Grafana snapshot. :thumbsup:
